A: Real patient endoscopic image of the gastric body in a case report of juvenile polyposis syndrome-associated gastric cancer, showing numerous densely distributed cystic polyps with normal coloration from cardia to antrum — a classic endoscopic manifestation of multiple gastric juvenile polyps in JPS. in_text_mentions: Upper gastrointestinal tract endoscopy revealed 5 polyps (Figure 1), and gastric polyps biopsies were submitted for histopathology. Submitted fragments exhibited moderate chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate of lymphocytes, negative for H pylori, and there was no metaplasia nor dysplasia. Colonoscopy illustrated multiple pedunculated polyps throughout the colon (Figure 2). This substantiated a diagnosis of JPS.

plate_findings.evidence: Macroscopic view showing diffuse gastric polyposis throughout the stomach; in-text: 'Macroscopic findings of the resected specimen showed diffuse gastric polyposis throughout the stomach.'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Gross specimen of the resected stomach from a JPS patient showing diffuse gastric polyposis, the classic macroscopic manifestation of gastric juvenile polyposis; arrows mark the JPS-associated adenocarcinoma and arrowheads the additional intramucosal carcinomas. B: Low-power H&E of the resected stomach showing multiple juvenile polyps with prominent stromal edema, the classic histologic picture of gastric juvenile polyps in JPS; human patient material of the target disease. C: H&E of the antral tumor showing well-differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma arising in a stomach with diffuse juvenile polyposis; the disease-focused article title ('Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome-Associated Gastric Cancer') together with the captioned manifestation supports JPS attribution, although adenocarcinoma is a complication rather than a defining feature, so confidence is moderated.

panels.figure_caption: Macroscopic and histopathological findings of the resected specimen. (A) Macroscopic view showing diffuse gastric polyposis throughout the stomach. Arrows indicate the 35-mm adenocarcinoma, while arrowheads indicate additional intramucosal adenocarcinomas measuring <10 mm. (B) Low-power histological findings of multiple polyps showing prominent stromal edema, consistent with juvenile polyps. (C) Histopathological findings showing a tumor composed of well-formed tubular structures resembling normal glands, consistent with well-differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma.
in_text_mentions: Macroscopic findings of the resected specimen showed diffuse gastric polyposis throughout the stomach. A 35-mm tumor was identified on the posterior wall of the antrum (Fig. 2A). Histopathological examination revealed multiple juvenile polyps in the background mucosa (Fig. 2B). The tumor located in the antrum was a well-differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma (Fig. 2C) with the following characteristics: L, Ant, 35 × 25 × 20 mm, type 0–IIa, tub1, pT1a (M), ly0, v0, pPM0, pDM0, pN0, cN0, and pStage IA. Four additional intramucosal carcinomas (pT1a), each <10 mm in size, were identified. Multiple
